hero.title: Useful systems, built in the open where practical.
hero.lede: Lowcountry Digital Works is still being established, so this page distinguishes what is live from what is actively being developed. The examples below show the kind of practical website and application work underway without presenting unfinished products as completed client engagements.

projects.name: Lowcountry Digital Works website
projects.description: The public LDW site is a lightweight, accessibility-tested static website with repository-controlled content, local brand assets, and Cloudflare edge delivery.
highlights: Automated browser and accessibility regression checks

projects.name: Document Control
projects.description: A configurable Lowcountry Digital Works product for structured document workflows, approvals, accountability, audit history, search, export, and administrative configuration.

projects.name: Secure Exchange
projects.description: A provider-neutral product for protected message and document exchange, queue-based staff workflows, lifecycle accountability, retention, and sanitized audit history. Current foundation work uses a customer-owned, isolated deployment model with an AWS-first reference architecture; production infrastructure is not yet provisioned.
highlights: Secure external intake and outbound delivery workflows
Individual workforce accountability and queue routing
Provider-neutral core with customer-owned deployment direction

technology.title: Technology chosen in proportion to the problem.
technology.lede: These are examples of tools and platforms currently used in Lowcountry Digital Works website, application, automation, and delivery work. A project does not inherit a platform simply because it appears here.

items.name: GitHub
items.description: Source control, review, and delivery workflows

items.name: Cloudflare
items.description: DNS, edge hosting, security, and deployment

technology.trademarkNote: Product names and marks are used only to identify technologies used in the work. Their owners do not sponsor or endorse Lowcountry Digital Works.

principle.title: The stack should serve the work, not become the work.
principle.body: A small static website, an offline tool, a serverless application, or a more involved workflow system can all be the right answer in different situations. The goal is to choose the simplest maintainable architecture that meets the actual requirements.
